projects.title: Clean wells for six hillside villages
projects.summary: Villagers walk up to two hours a day for water. This project drills and maintains six shallow wells, run by local water committees.
projects.quote: Now my daughter is at school before the bell, not carrying jerrycans.
projects.story:
## The problem

In the dry season, families in the six hillside villages above Lake Tanganyika rely on a single seasonal stream. Children, mostly girls, make the trip before school and often arrive late or not at all.

## What we're doing

Each well is sited with the village water committee, drilled by a local crew, and fitted with a hand pump that can be repaired with parts sold in Kigoma town. Committees collect a small monthly fee that covers repairs.

## Long-term impact

Within a year of a well opening, school attendance in the first pilot village rose noticeably, and clinic visits for waterborne illness fell.

updates.title: Third well is running
updates.body: The Mwamgongo well passed its water-quality test and opened to the village on Saturday.

updates.title: Committee training finished
updates.body: Twenty-four committee members completed pump repair and bookkeeping training.

projects.title: Reading corners in rural primary schools
projects.summary: Stocking 20 classrooms with books in Spanish and Tsotsil, and training teachers to run daily reading time.
projects.quote: The children argue over who gets the shelf first in the morning.
projects.story:
## The problem

Many rural schools have textbooks but no books children choose to read for fun, and almost nothing in their home language.

## What we're doing

Each classroom gets a shelf of 180 books, a reading mat, and a teacher trained to run 20 minutes of daily free reading. Local authors translate picture books into Tsotsil.

## Long-term impact

Students who read daily for a full year improved reading fluency well beyond the regional average.

updates.title: Twelve new shelves installed
updates.body: Schools in Chenalhó received their reading corners before the new term.

projects.title: Mobile clinic for remote river communities
projects.summary: A boat clinic that visits 14 riverside communities every month with a nurse, a midwife and basic medicines.
projects.quote: We know the boat comes on the second Tuesday. People wait at the bank.
projects.story:
## The problem

The nearest hospital is a two-day boat ride for most communities along the upper river.

## What we're doing

A converted cargo boat carries a nurse and a midwife on a fixed monthly route, with prenatal checks, vaccinations and a radio link to a doctor in Iquitos.

## Long-term impact

Regular visits mean problems are caught early, and expectant mothers have a plan before labor begins.

updates.title: New solar fridge on board
updates.body: Vaccines can now stay cold for the full nine-day route.

projects.title: Seed banks for women farmers
projects.summary: Community seed banks that store drought-tolerant millet and sorghum, managed by women's farming groups.
projects.quote: The seed belongs to us now, not to the trader.
projects.story:
## The problem

After a poor harvest, farmers often eat their seed stock and must buy expensive seed on credit the next season.

## What we're doing

Each group builds a sealed storage room and lends seed to members, who return it with a small share after harvest.

## Long-term impact

Groups now hold reserves through a bad year and choose varieties suited to their own fields.

updates.title: Harvest returns recorded
updates.body: Members returned 94% of borrowed seed after the early millet harvest.

projects.title: Neighborhood repair café
projects.summary: Volunteer fixers repair lamps, bikes and clothes for free once a month at the local library.
projects.quote: I came in with a broken toaster and left knowing three new people.
projects.story:
## The problem

Small household items get thrown out because repairs cost more than replacing them.

## What we're doing

Volunteers with sewing, electrical and bike skills sit with each visitor and fix the item together, so people learn as they go.

## Long-term impact

Fewer items go to landfill, and neighbors meet people they would not otherwise talk to.

updates.title: Bike stand donated
updates.body: A local shop donated a second repair stand for the bike table.

projects.title: Mangrove replanting along the delta
projects.summary: Fishing families replant mangroves that protect the coast from storm surge and bring back fish nurseries.
projects.quote: My grandfather fished here. Now my son may too.
projects.story:
## The problem

Decades of clearing left villages exposed to storm surge, and fish catches dropped as nursery habitat disappeared.

## What we're doing

Villagers raise seedlings in nurseries and plant them at low tide, paid per surviving tree after twelve months.

## Long-term impact

Replanted stretches already show crab and juvenile fish returning.

updates.title: One-year survival count
updates.body: 71% of last year's seedlings survived the monsoon season.
